assumptions: The opportunity is scored at its current planning stage, with competent execution and extensive AI assistance, but without assuming any unrecorded regulator sponsorship, operator commitment, or procurement access.
The proposed 60000-200000 PLN annual operator pricing, 65-80% gross margin, and 90000 PLN initial-capital estimate are hypotheses rather than validated economics.

A gambling-policy lead, specialist privacy counsel, security expertise, and public-affairs support can be hired or contracted, but their cost and the founder time needed to coordinate them remain uncertain.
The founder company would be a technology and operations supplier rather than a gambling operator, and a credible independent or regulator-recognized entity would hold the data-governance mandate.

The reviewed evidence establishes neither a present Polish cross-operator mandate nor a legally unobtainable mandate; sponsorship is therefore treated as a high-impact unknown rather than a fatal fact.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A written sponsor commitment from the relevant Polish authority or credible operator association; a specialist legal opinion defining lawful basis, controller roles, withdrawal and appeals; binding paid-pilot or conditional rollout commitments from several material operators; and a costed model showing integration expense, security and uptime burden, price, margin, procurement timing, retention, and a conservative founder-net-worth path.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The concept correctly identifies self-exclusion as a coordination and governance problem rather than merely an operator feature. Poland's operator-level controls, the EU recommendation, and compulsory British and Swedish schemes support the insight that portable coverage requires a recognized shared rail. The insight is useful but not novel, and the foreign precedents also reveal that the decisive asset is public authority rather than the software itself.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Cross-operator exclusion addresses a consequential player-protection and regulatory gap, and a sponsor could value auditable nationwide coverage. However, the paying operators can already point to internal exclusion controls, may lose gambling revenue when exclusion becomes more effective, and have shown no willingness to fund the proposed rail or pricing. The social pain is clearer than payer urgency.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A mandatory registration-and-login check could produce recurring usage, high retention, and software-like operating leverage. Against that, there are only 17 listed private online-betting operators, pricing and usage fees are unvalidated, and high-availability infrastructure, identity resolution, audits, insurance, legal governance, security, and support will consume meaningful margin. Even full adoption at the stated membership range does not yet establish an evidence-backed path to 5 million PLN of founder net worth, especially if a sponsoring or public-interest body captures much of the economics.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: The initial segment is exceptionally clear and bounded: a sponsor plus 17 licensed private online-betting operators. That concentration makes the deployment surface manageable, but it also caps buyer count, increases buyer power, and leaves state-monopoly online casino and number games outside the immediately addressable private market. The beachhead is policy-meaningful but not yet shown to be commercially large enough on its own.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: If one rail becomes the regulator-recognized default, nationwide coverage, integrations, and audit acceptance could create a winner-take-most position. The current candidate does not control that designation, and a ministry, association, public tender winner, established identity provider, or operator consortium could own or replace the infrastructure. Domination potential is strong only after winning an institutional control point that is presently uncommitted.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven Polish rail could extend into additional gambling channels, compliance reporting, safer-gambling workflows, or reusable national deployments elsewhere in CEE. Yet each adjacent jurisdiction requires its own lawful basis, sponsor, governance, procurement, operator integrations, and political coalition, so the initial win would provide credibility and technical reuse but not automatic distribution.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Regulatory recognition, trusted governance, identity-match quality, operator integrations, audited uptime, and accumulated operating history could create substantial switching costs and durable incumbency. Those advantages would compound after adoption. They are conditional, however: the founder does not currently own the mandate, and a sponsor could tender, internalize, or reassign the utility while retaining the governance and relationship moat.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: For an excluded player and the regulator, one portable status checked across operators is materially more effective and convenient than repeating account-specific exclusions. A minimized yes-or-no API is also more privacy-conscious than sharing wagering history or an addiction score. The advantage is less compelling to operators absent compulsion because it adds integration, liability, and lost-play costs without a demonstrated financial return beyond enhanced compliance.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: National schemes abroad prove feasibility, and EU policy provides a favorable conceptual precedent. But the cited EU recommendation dates to 2014, the current Polish statute still specifies operator-level controls, and the research identifies no new Polish legislative, procurement, enforcement, or association initiative that creates an adoption window now. The direction is plausible; the immediate catalyst is missing.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The target-account list is small, but access is not equivalent to adoption. The route requires ministry, regulator, or association sponsorship before ordinary operator selling can work, while operator incentives are mixed and successful comparators rely on compulsory participation. Long policy, coalition, legal, and procurement cycles are difficult to validate cheaply and conflict with the founder's preference for low-social-intensity, part-time execution.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The underlying API and audit system are technically feasible and align with the founder's data background, but production success requires specialist gambling law, GDPR controller design, identity matching, appeals, security certification, breach and false-match liability management, high availability, institutional sales, and public affairs. A 90000 PLN budget and roughly three founder hours per day appear tight before sponsorship, and the hardest capabilities are legal and relational rather than tasks AI can reliably substitute.

highest_value_structural_change: Separate public-interest governance from commercial execution: require a regulator- or association-backed independent controller to own the exclusion mandate and rules, while the founder company becomes the contracted, reusable white-label technology and operations provider. Do not fund the national build until that sponsor secures binding anchor-operator participation and a paid pilot; design the platform so the same minimized-status infrastructure can be licensed into additional jurisdictions rather than relying on Poland's 17 operators alone.
main_structural_strength: A regulator-recognized national status rail could turn one integration into the default compliance checkpoint for a concentrated licensed market, creating recurring checks, high switching costs, and winner-take-most infrastructure economics.
primary_score_limiter: The company cannot create its own essential control point: without regulator, ministry, or credible association authority that supplies a lawful governance model and binding operator participation, coverage, willingness to pay, recurrence, and defensibility all remain hypothetical.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The reviewed Polish statute provides operator-level responsible-gambling controls but no shared-registry mandate, while the successful British and Swedish comparators obtain cross-operator coverage through licence or statutory obligations; an incumbent Polish operator already offers its own account-specific exclusion.
